subject: Information Theory
title: Dictionary Compression
description: A quick win: understand Dictionary Compression.

hook.text: The word 'the' appears 69,000 times in Moby Dick. Dictionary compression stores it once, references it everywhere.

buildup.text: LZ77 and LZ78 (Lempel-Ziv) build dictionaries of repeated patterns during compression.

discovery.text: When a pattern recurs, the compressor outputs a pointer instead of the data. Pointers are shorter.

twist.text: The dictionary builds itself adaptively—no prior knowledge of the data needed. It learns as it compresses.

climax.text: ZIP, gzip, and PNG all use LZ variants. They dominate general-purpose lossless compression.

punchline.text: Store the pattern once. Point to it forever.

quiz.question: How does LZ compression reduce file size?
options: By replacing repeated patterns with short references
